10.1002_adma.74786: Efficient wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells are essential for high‐performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs), yet their fabrication in humid ambient air remains difficult because moisture‐ and oxygen‐induced reactions deteriorate film quality and stability. Here, 4‐[[4,6‐bis(octylthio)‐1,3,5‐triazin‐2‐yl]amino]‐2,6‐bis(1,1‐dimethylethyl)‐phenol (BTDP) is introduced into the perovskite precursor to enable WBG perovskite formation under high‐humid ambient air conditions. BTDP scavenges superoxide radical anions, inhibits I − oxidation to I 2 , absorbs ultraviolet light, coordinates with Pb 2+ to regulate crystallization and forms a hydrophobic barrier at surfaces and grain boundaries. With this strategy, blade‐coated WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated at 60% relative humidity deliver a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.45%, which represents the highest PCE reported for air‐processed WBG PSCs with bandgap ≥1.68 eV. Mini‐modules with an aperture area of 14.81 cm 2 reach 20.12% efficiency. Moreover, the method enables ambient‐air fabrication of two‐terminal perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) TSCs with a certified efficiency of 32.59%, among the highest PCEs reported for two‐terminal perovskite/TOPCon TSCs. This study provides a scalable route to efficient, stable single‐junction and tandem perovskite photovoltaics.
10.1002_aenm.71338: Accurate lifetime prediction is critical for the reliable use of lithium‐ion batteries. However, batteries at early stage commonly show consistent electrical behaviors impeding distinguishing their future life trends. In this work, the internal strain is monitored in‐situ by implanting fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors into 18 cells belonging to 3 different electrochemical systems. We find the internal strain at the formation stage exhibits a biphasic feature attributed to the dynamic competition between solid‐phase growth and gas‐phase accumulation. The SEI formation strain (SFS) is further found to be linked closely to the thickness and compactness of SEI which influence the degradation path of battery. The high correlation between SFS and capacity loss is further explored to build an elastic net model for battery lifetime prediction, achieving a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.40%. This work presents a new avenue for understanding the mechanism of SEI formation and predicting the battery lifetime at the ultra‐early formation stage.
10.1016_j.seppur.2026.140501: Osmotically assisted reverse osmosis (OARO) extends membrane-based brine concentration by reducing the effective osmotic pressure difference across the membrane. This study develops a process-level stagewise projection framework for brine-split OARO using a commercial Toyobo hollow-fibre membrane module and experimentally assesses selected local operating conditions. In this configuration, part of the final brine is redirected to the sweep side. The framework calculates feed- and sweep-side concentrations, flow rates, membrane-transferred water flow, salt transport and pressure requirements. The projection was applied to a 70 g/L NaCl feed at 230 L/h with a target concentration of 316 g/L. At a brine-split factor of 55%, the framework yielded a nine-stage configuration operating at about 67 bar with a feed-side pumping specific energy consumption of 2.40 kWh/m 3 of process feed. Seven- and eight-stage configurations reached approximately 291 and 307 g/L, respectively, while operating at the 70 bar module pressure limit. Increasing the brine-split factor from 45 to 60% reduced feed-side pumping specific energy consumption from 2.51 to 2.34 kWh/m 3 but increased sweep-outlet salinity from approximately 37 to 47 g/L. Six selected local stage conditions were reproduced experimentally using a single OARO module. The framework captured the main trends in membrane-transferred water flow, concentration development and flow redistribution, with a root-mean-square error of 3.24 L/h for water transfer. Deviations were larger in the high-concentration region. The results support the framework as a computationally efficient tool for preliminary stagewise sizing of brine-split OARO systems approaching NaCl saturation.
